# Duckpad 0.15.0
**Remote SSH File** and **Log Tail Viewer** bring read-only server files and live logs into Duckpad, alongside faster Find input and consistent native controls.
## Remote SSH File
- Choose **File → Open Remote File…** (**Control-Command-O**) to browse servers using macOS OpenSSH configuration, SSH keys and the agent. Search configured/recent hosts, navigate folders, show hidden files, preview contents and open multiple files without closing the browser. - Reuse one SSH connection for browsing, previews and files on the same host. Transport failures receive three bounded retries, followed by a manual Retry action when needed. Cancelling one request preserves other files using the connection. - Use **Command-L** for the remote path, **Shift-Command-L** for the host, **Command-R** to refresh, **Command-Up** for the parent folder and **Command-W** to close the browser. These commands stay in the browser while it has focus. - Long remote paths expand with the window. Inputs, dropdown rows, navigation and action buttons share Duckpad's themes, neutral hover/focus feedback and aligned icon controls.
## Log Tail Viewer
- Open a saved local file and choose **View → Tail Mode**, or enable **Follow file changes (Tail)** when opening a remote file. New output follows the end until you scroll up; collection continues while following is paused. Follow End returns to the newest output, with an unread-line count while paused. - Follow file rotation and truncation, retain incomplete UTF-8 characters until the next read, and preserve each split pane's selection and viewport. Clear Output clears only the viewer; it never deletes the source log. Stop exits observation without writing to the source. - Automatically recognize common log files and highlight timestamps, severity fields and stack-trace headers. The shared Log language also displays supported ANSI SGR colours and text attributes while retaining the original bytes. Choose Plain Text to reveal raw escape sequences.
## Other improvements
- Keep English and Korean Find input responsive when large wrapped files with word-occurrence markers remain open in other tabs. Incremental match counts avoid building hidden Find All result rows and unnecessary dialog resizing. - Workspace folders offer **Reveal in Terminal** and **Reveal in Embedded Terminal**. Embedded Terminal opens a new session in that folder and preserves existing shells. - Reuse common search/action/icon components for hover, pressed and disabled states. Correct native icon alignment insets so Tail toolbar hover areas stay centered inside the bar. - Localize the new commands, controls, status messages and errors in all eight supported languages.
App and helpers: **0.15.0 (66)**, upgrading **0.14.3 (65)**. Requires **macOS 13 or later**. The universal distribution supports Apple Silicon and Intel. Existing settings, recovery data, encodings, Undo history and the native plugin ABI remain compatible. No new dependencies or separately installed Ghostty or ripgrep application are required.
## Installation
Download `Duckpad-0.15.0-universal.dmg` and drag Duckpad into Applications, or extract `Duckpad-0.15.0-universal.zip`. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Existing installations can use Check for Updates after the signed update feed is published.
## Validation and limitations
**188 distinct focused Release test functions completed**, including two opt-in real SSH tests and three explicitly enabled performance checks. Coverage includes SSH protocol/path quoting, shared connections and cancellation, bounded retry, UTF-8 boundaries, file rotation, read-only restrictions and recovery, native log/ANSI styling, Find and Korean composition, terminal routing, and control geometry across eight languages. Native light/dark snapshots verify dropdown hover, long paths and centered Tail controls. The final universal package is verified and exercised with isolated packaged smoke checks before publication. Native Save-panel automation is skipped.
On the local Apple Silicon validation machine, 48,000-byte appends on a 17.5 MB shared document measured **4.10 ms maximum** over 12 samples. Find input with three cached 8 MB wrapped documents and 100,000 markers each measured **6.47 ms maximum** over seven marked-text updates. Immediate append/layout/display for the shared, wrapped 8.44 MB ANSI fixture measured **2.67 ms maximum** over six appends; subsequent asynchronous colouring is outside that measurement. Network time is excluded.
One existing asynchronous browser test process exits with code 0 before its completion marker; its cause is undiagnosed and it is not counted as passed. A standalone native harness owning `NSApp.run` separately completed the same bounded-preview, multiple-open and stale-navigation workflow. The remaining affected UI checks completed in individual runs.
Remote access is read-only and UTF-8 only. Password prompts are not supported; use SSH configuration, keys or an agent, and trust a new host in Terminal before connecting. Duckpad does not automatically accept unknown host keys. Servers need a POSIX shell, `stat` (GNU or BSD), `tail` and `head`. Remote snapshots are limited to 64 MiB; Tail starts with the latest 1 MiB and allows 64 MiB of growth before Clear Output is required. Polling defaults to 250 ms locally and one second remotely; network latency is separate. Copy-truncate followed by regrowth beyond the old cursor between polls cannot be distinguished from an append. Restored Tail tabs start paused and reconnect on request.
Log detection and ANSI interpretation are bounded, generic highlighting rather than a terminal emulator or a complete grammar for every log library. Unsupported escape families remain raw text. Explicit source RGB colours can have poor contrast. There is no universal 50 ms rendering guarantee: an 18.9 MB single-line Unicode ANSI fixture previously measured 53.8–66.1 ms for first colour layout, and publishing 100,000 search highlights measured approximately 51.8 ms. These known stress limits are retained; network time and initial whole-file loading are separate from incremental append measurements.
Intel hardware, macOS 13 runtime, Linux server execution, external production SSH servers, physical Korean keyboard interaction and the full repository test suite are not validated. The distribution is ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID signing or Apple notarization.
## Published distribution validation
- Source: `52d4b8a878b50ab8b318547590cbcda99b99f2de` from [PR #97](https://github.com/namJeongwan/duckpad/pull/97); the clean build tree matches the merged main tree. - Universal app and all three Duckpad helpers: **0.15.0 (66)** with **arm64 + x86_64** slices; bundle/resource/signature verification passed. - Isolated final-package checks passed: Finder/Open With, saved access after relaunch, window resizing, sandboxed extension/XPC isolation, bundled ripgrep, native languages and Log/ANSI styling. - Final sandboxed SSH check passed through the authenticated helper: aliases, directory browsing, bounded preview, multiple files and split-byte Korean/emoji Tail used exactly **one** authenticated SSH transport. No fixture SSH clients survived app exit. - DMG verification and ZIP integrity checks passed. SHA-256 checksums are attached. - Native Save-panel automation was skipped. Intel hardware, macOS 13 runtime, external/Linux servers, physical Korean keyboard interaction and the full test suite remain unvalidated. Ad-hoc signed; not Apple notarized.
